system.name: VTM (Visual Token Matching)
system.one_liner: A universal few-shot learner for dense prediction that matches patch tokens of a query image to support image and label tokens at several feature levels.

content.variant_note: a tall hierarchical encoder-decoder with aligned levels, plus two side panels that expand the Token Matching Module and the Fusion Block
content.argues: Non-parametric matching of query and support tokens at every feature level, with a few task-specific parameters, handles arbitrary dense tasks in one architecture.
content.subject: The architecture: image encoder, label encoder, four Token Matching modules, a Fusion chain with a Head, and zoomed views of two modules.

Given the query image and the support set, the image encoder first extracts patch-level embeddings (tokens)

summary: Visual Token Matching (VTM) is a universal few-shot learner for dense prediction tasks: it matches patch tokens of a query image to those of a few support image and label pairs at several feature levels, and adapts to a new task with a few task-specific parameters. Figure 1 draws the model as a tall hierarchical encoder-decoder in four columns: a blue image encoder shared by query and support images, a pink label encoder, four orange Token Matching modules, and lavender Fusion blocks with a Head that give the predicted label. Red squares mark the task-specific parameters. Two panels on the right expand the Token Matching Module (linear maps, scaled dot-product attention) and the Fusion Block.
